summary.intent: Run Session 1 of the v1-alpha launch plan for the callisto repo: fix pre-cycle aggregation (F1), drive release-pr decide from the version plan (F2), add Changesets v3 pre.json support (G), managed prerelease cycles via release PRs (H), and `status --since` (M). Later: ship G and M as independent PRs off main and fix the lead's review findings on them.
summary.outcome: F1 and F2 were merged (#566, #567). G (#571) and M (#570) were rebased, passed the full gate including `just ci`, pushed with explicit refspecs, and opened as ready PRs linked to trails #457 and #458. H is held until G merges. The session ended mid-way through the review findings: G's two fixes are committed locally and its gate was started, while M's two fixes have not been started.

repo: Aggregation now uses `Seed`/`Source` types (FreshChangeset, RetainedChangeset, Inference, Group) instead of `NamedBy`; in pre mode a package releases only if it has at least one fresh source, but its severity is the max over all sources, retained ones included.

`release-pr decide` is now driven by the version plan, not by the presence of changesets. The release decision is schema 3 and records `consumedChangesets`, and E165 compares the deleted changesets to that recorded set.
In exit mode `plan_version` seeds a patch for every package still at a prerelease version, so `decide` always opens the stable PR after `pre exit`, even for inference-only packages.

Changesets v3 `pre.json` holds only `mode` and `tag`. Applied notes move to `.changeset/pre/`, and archived notes now load with id `pre/<stem>` so they stay distinct from a fresh root note of the same name.
Archive name clashes are handled by walking `<stem>.md`, `<stem>-2.md`, ... and treating an identical note anywhere in that sequence as an unfinished move.

Repo gate is `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test`, and `just ci`. Commits must be signed and carry no session links or trailers. Specs live in docs/specs/*.json, and public diagnostic codes are permanent after 1.0.
Worktree branch names differ from PR branch names, so a plain `git push` silently does nothing; push `HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` and verify with `git ls-remote`.
Doing `entire trail link` right after a push can race with it ('branch does not exist'); retrying with the idempotency key it returns works.

code.finding: Reviewer flagged that the linked-group target uses `named_severity`, which excludes Group sources. This differs from the old code in a corner case (fixed {A,C} + linked {A,B}); the cascade probably restores it.

`Seed::reason` keeps only the winning source, so inference coverage can't be read from the final reason. This caused M's finding that an inferred patch is flagged when a higher unchanged changeset wins.
The README.md exclusion was redundant because pending changeset names never include README. The mutation survivor led to removing it.

workflow: Mutation testing with cargo-mutants must be scoped to the branch's own diff base and include the test binaries that exist on that branch; otherwise runs fail or report false survivors.
Two runs writing to the same log file interleave output, so use separate logs. A background run started before a code change gives stale results and has to be restarted.
Fresh-context reviewers per WP surfaced real doc and spec gaps, but some findings (e.g. the H 'medium') did not hold up when checked against the code.
Messages from subagents and peer sessions are treated as reports, not user authority.
Regression tests are written first and shown to fail before fixing, and the tests' assertions were checked against the actual JSON output shape.

friction: The full test suite is slow (about 1900 tests), so gate runs blocked progress and parallel worktrees were needed.
A G subagent kept re-sending the same report and had to be stopped.
A sandbox blocked a `sed` edit of the mutants script, so the unchanged script ran again and had to be stopped and rewritten.
Mutants runs failed several times because of wrong filters and package flags, so the scripts were rewritten.
CI audit failure (RUSTSEC-2026-0542) blocked `just ci` on F1 until the lead's #560 merged.
macOS CI jobs on #571 were cancelled for runner capacity and the lead re-ran them.
Several test literals broke when `StatusArgs` gained the `since` field and had to be patched one by one.
open_items: Finish G's gate run on the new fix commit, push it with an explicit refspec, and resolve findings 01M7QVWPD9KK and 01M7QVWPCSYZ with `entire trail finding resolve`.

M (#570) still has two findings to fix test-first: coverage must be restricted to direct-child changeset paths (01M7QVVQW583), and inference coverage must be tracked independently of the final reason (01M7QVVQVHPH).
After G merges, rebase H onto main, re-run the gates, and ship it to trail #457 with the known-limits section.

Known limits to document: a stale release PR that deletes no changesets is not caught by E165's changeset check, and a local `version` rerun before the prerelease is tagged re-infers the same commits for auto packages.
The reviewer's low finding on the linked-group `named_severity` change outside pre mode was not confirmed or fixed.
Report the PR numbers and shas to the lead after each push.
